terms.gloss: camp out, sleep in a tent
terms.comment: Our phrase, and a verb: Latin says what one does. Sub pellibus, “under hides”, is Caesar’s and Livy’s for soldiers living in tents, which were made of leather; pernoctāre is to spend the night. We have found no word for camping as a pastime; Traupman gives only the camp ground and the tent.

phrases.english: he decided to winter in tents (Caesar, of his army)
to sleep out under the open sky

sources: Lewis & Short: pellis · Lewis & Short: pernocto · Lewis & Short: divum
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 286, 392 (campsite and tent; no word for camping). Morgan–Owens has only the camping stove.
